I've put together a concise MAP and owner matrix (attached: MAP-AverySystems-20270712.pdf) and a short action-items workbook. High level:

1) API keys (owner: Redwood Platform Ops / Monica)
   - We will create env-scoped API keys for you (dev/staging/prod simulated).
   - Keys can be scoped by route and rotated via Console; we will provide CLI steps and a curl example.

2) Redwood org setup (owner: Monica + Sean)
   - We need one org admin invite for your infra lead and one read-only for PMs.
   - Please provide emails for the invites; we will send Org invite links that expire in 72 hours.

3) IP allowlist (owner: Avery for firewall rules, Redwood provides egress list)
   - See Marissa's technical note for recommended outbound IPs. We will also enable prefix-based ranges for CIDR blocks where possible.

4) VPC peering (owner: Avery infra + Redwood network team / Marissa)
   - Required: BGP is not needed; static routes acceptable. We recommend a non-overlapping /24 allocation on your side for peering.
   - Peering handshake: share VPC ID, preferred region, and a contact for peering acceptance.

Proposed timeline (assuming we receive the items below by Thu 2027-07-15):
- Fri 07/16: Redwood provisions API keys and sends org invites
- Mon 07/19: Networking test (IP allowlist + simple ping/health check)
- Tue 07/20: VPC peering complete; smoke tests
- Wed 07/21: Full POC kickoff and scripted load test begins (3 weeks)

Please confirm owners and whether the proposed dates work. I've attached the MAP PDF and an action-items workbook (MAP-action-items.xlsx). Also looping Marissa for technical specifics on IPs and peering.

Evan / Monica — adding a few technical constraints and example configs so your infra team can estimate effort. Quick notes below, attached is a small snippet file (vpc-peering-snippets.txt).

IP allowlist / egress
- Primary outbound IP set (us-west-2): 54.182.120.0/24, 3.101.45.0/24 (we publish these ranges for the POC).
- If you require granular per-route IPs, we can provide per-cluster prefixes but that may add ~24 hours.

VPC peering notes
- Required: non-overlapping IP space. We recommend your peering subnet be a /24 (e.g., 10.20.30.0/24).
- Route tables: add a route for Redwood peer CIDR pointing to the peering connection; no transitive routing supported (standard cloud provider limitation).
- Egress: if your VMs are behind NAT and need outbound access to our API, ensure SNAT preserves source mapping or allow our egress pair in your firewall.

Ports & protocols
- Recommended: allow outbound TCP 443 to our endpoints. For health-check callbacks we use HTTPS POST on 443 and occasional TLS 1.2/1.3 handshakes. No special UDP ports required.

Sample verification flow (for your infra team)
- Step 1: Provide VPC ID + region + peering contact
- Step 2: Redwood initiates peering request (we will provide the peer account id)
- Step 3: Your team accepts; both sides update route tables
- Step 4: Run connectivity test (curl https://status.redwood-inference.com/health from a bastion host)

Attachments: vpc-peering-snippets.txt (contains Terraform examples, route table commands, and a tiny curl health-check script). Happy to jump on a 30-min ops call if you'd like to walk through.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
